matches.rationale: The ground truth flags that the operation p⊙_t q (and its generating definition via Definition 2.6) is incorrectly defined/expressed, undermining downstream results. Findings 2, 3, 4, 5, and 7 all independently identify that this operation (odot_t, derived from Definition 2.6) fails to have the claimed algebraic properties — specifically that t is an absorbing element, breaking group/semigroup structure, closure of Z*, and the ultrafilter-extension reasoning in Theorems 3.3, 3.5, and 4.3 — which is exactly the symptom of a faulty operation definition cascading through the paper.

pred_verdicts.rationale: Flags an issue with Definition 2.4 (elementary symmetric polynomial), a different definitional claim not covered by the ground truth about p⊙_t q.

Directly identifies that the odot_{l,k} operation defined via Definition 2.6 lacks the claimed group structure (absorbing element), matching the GT's defect about the operation's definition being incorrect.
Shows the operation p⊙_t q produces absorbing/degenerate behavior at t, invalidating Theorem 3.3, a direct symptom of the flawed operation definition.
Demonstrates Z* is not closed under odot_t, showing the operation's definition/extension is broken, consistent with the GT defect.
Further exposes the same absorbing-element flaw in odot_t causing Theorem 3.5 to fail, another manifestation of the same operation-definition defect.
Targets a different logical flaw (invalid central-set argument) in the proof of Theorem 3.4, not the definition of p⊙_t q itself.
Directly discusses the notation p⊙_t q and an invalid inference stemming from its improperly characterized structure, matching the GT defect.
Points to a sign-inconsistency in the proof of Theorem 4.7 unrelated to the core definition of p⊙_t q.
Identifies an algebraic expansion error specific to the l=1,k=-1 case in Theorem 4.10/Corollary 4.12, a distinct numerical instance not matching the GT's p⊙_t q locus.
Flags use of an undefined operation oplus_{l,k} in Corollaries 4.12/4.14, a separate notational defect not covered by the ground truth.
